subject: Auxiliary surge allocation & pricing worksheet
messages:
From: Sarah Avery <sarah.avery@averysys.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@averysys.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool — burst headroom + commercial fit

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. A few follow-ups from our infra and procurement teams as we size a Dedicated pool for our inference workloads:

- We expect steady-state of ~80 v100-equivalent tokens/sec with 5k concurrent short requests during business hours, plus 20–30 minute peak windows 2–3x/day.
- We want a firm throughput guarantee for steady-state (SLA) and a predictable model for short bursts (surge headroom) — ideally something we can model into our SRE runbooks.
- Questions: How do you size the GPU pool for headroom vs committed capacity? What are typical cooldowns and surge-rate multipliers? How does pricing for the burst add-on work (per-minute top-up, slabed credits, or % over commit)?

Can you share a worksheet with pricing scenarios and a recommended guardrail config (cooldown, max burst duration, governor)? Procurement also needs an initial ballpark for a 12-month reserved commit.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a call if that’s easier.

Best,
Sarah
Head of ML Infrastructure
Avery Systems

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Avery <sarah.avery@averysys.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — burst headroom + commercial fit

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear context. I put together a short worksheet that lays out three sizing + pricing scenarios (Conservative, Targeted, Flexible) and paired surge models (credit pack, per-minute top-up, and proportional slab). See attached: avery-dedicated-pricing-worksheet-v2.xlsx and a short SLA matrix (sla-throughput-matrix.pdf).

High level answers up front:
- Pool sizing: we recommend sizing committed capacity to handle your steady-state plus 20% headroom for short tail latency. For your numbers that maps to ~1.2–1.4x steady capacity depending on model footprint.
- Burst governance: default cooldown is 15m after a sustained surge; max continuous burst window 30m with up to 3 consecutive bursts allowed before manual review.
- Surge pricing: our standard option is a prepaid credit pool (cheaper per-token) or on-demand per-minute overlay (no commit, higher unit price). For committed customers we also offer a burst-credit multiplier discount tied to reserved commit size.

I’ll copy Karthik and Markus for pricing validation and Monica for ops runbook suggestions. If it helps, I can sketch a mutual action plan (MAP) and a 30/60/90 rollout showing how we throttle to protect SLOs while you ramp.

Would you like a 30-minute call Wed morning to walk through the worksheet?

Thanks —
Aisha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Dedicated GPU pool — burst headroom + commercial fit

Aisha / team — quick internal notes after skimming the worksheet:

- Pricing buckets: the worksheet currently shows 3 burst options (credit pack, per-minute top-up, and a capped overlay). Recommend we emphasize the capped overlay for Avery — it prevents runaway spend and maps cleanly to their SRE request for predictable headroom.
- Discounting: For a 12-month reserved commit at 50% of forecast steady-state we can layer a 18% reserved discount + 30% on burst-credit bundles. If they want a higher commit we can push to 22% + 40% on bursts (needs approval from finance).
- Cooldown: 15m default OK; propose a 10m short-burst path for <5m surges (lower rate) and 30m cooldown after >30m sustained surge. This gives ops more granular control. Monica — can you add recommended governor thresholds (CPU/RAM/KV cache hit rates) to the worksheet?

Markus — if we present the capped overlay pricing, confirm margin floor and whether we can commit to the burst discount tiers above.

-Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 12:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Dedicated GPU pool — burst headroom + commercial fit

Team —

Confirmed: margin permits the 18% reserved / 30% burst-credit stack for the 50% commit baseline. For the 22% / 40% tier we need legal to sign off on a minimum revenue commitment (one-off) to protect us on long tail usage — propose a $25k minimum ARR guarantee for the higher burst discount.

Also, recommend we include a surge-safety clause: when a customer consumes >500% of commit for >45m we reserve the right to throttle to protect platform stability; we will notify and provide an emergency top-up path.

Monica — please add operational guardrails and a short blurb about the automatic fallback to smaller model variants during sustained surge windows (helps keep latency SLOs intact).

-Markus
VP Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Avery <sarah.avery@averysys.com>, procurement@averysys.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com, markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — burst headroom + commercial fit

Sarah / procurement team —

Thanks for the ask — attached is the worksheet you requested (avery-dedicated-pricing-worksheet-v2.xlsx) and a short SLA matrix. Key proposal summary:

- Committed capacity: 12-month reserve sized at 1.1x your steady-state (~50% of forecasted peak), discounted at 18%.
- Burst model: capped overlay (recommended) with a prepaid credit pack option. Overlay pricing: standard overlay = 2.4x unit rate of committed token; prepaid credit pack = 1.6x unit rate but requires prepayment and has a 12-month expiry.
- Cooldown / guardrails: short-burst path (<5m) uses 1.5x overlay and has a 10m cooldown. Long-burst path up to 30m uses 2.4x with automatic fallback and 30m cooldown; >30m sustained will trigger ops review and possible progressive throttling.
- Safety and SLAs: we include a surge-safety clause limiting emergency consumption >500% for >45m (we will notify and propose emergency top-up). Throughput SLA for steady-state tokens/sec with 99.95% uptime in region.

Next steps: if the high-level looks good I’ll schedule a 30-minute scoping call and circulate a MAP. Procurement, can you share any required PO terms or timing constraints?

Attachments: avery-dedicated-pricing-worksheet-v2.xlsx (pricing scenarios), sla-throughput-matrix.pdf (SLA & throughput guarantees)

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
